intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an open-air sunrise yoga session overlooking the lush Campuhan valley, followed by a peaceful walk along the scenic ridge trail through rice paddies and jungle. A perfect blend of mindfulness and nature immersion.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson with a local instructor on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, then unwind and watch one of Bali's legendary sunsets with a fresh coconut in hand.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Bali's world-renowned yoga culture with daily classes at The Yoga Barn, offering Hatha, Vinyasa, and Yin sessions in open-air jungle pavilions. Includes access to meditation workshops and healing circles over multiple sessions.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Crystal-Clear Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at Nusa Dua's pristine white-sand beaches, known for calm turquoise waters perfect for snorkeling and swimming. Rent a sun lounger, explore the coral reefs, and enjoy fresh grilled seafood from beachside warungs.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Organic Farm Visit
experiences.description: Visit a traditional organic farm in the Ubud highlands to hand-pick fresh ingredients, then learn to prepare authentic Balinese dishes like satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding under the guidance of a local chef. A deeply cultural and flavorful experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take a pre-booked budget airport shuttle or shared taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at a nearby warung (local Indonesian eatery) near the resort — try nasi goreng (fried rice) for under $3 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid overpriced taxis at night. Keep some Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) handy for small expenses. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and take your first stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the warm Bali morning air (around 25°C). Watch local fishermen and take in the coastal scenery. If the resort offers a free or low-cost yoga session on the beach, join it for a peaceful start.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach area — rent a surfboard or bodyboard from a local vendor (approx. $5–8/hour) and enjoy the waves. Walk along the shoreline and visit nearby beach warungs for a cold coconut.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby night market or local strip for dinner. Explore the surrounding neighborhood on foot and pick up any essentials at a local minimart (Indomaret or Alfamart).

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a simple breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — banana pancakes and fresh fruit juice for around $3–4.
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut and local snacks from a beachside vendor — budget $2–3.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local warung — try mie goreng (fried noodles) or satay skewers with rice for $3–5.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at a reputable money changer in town rather than at the airport for better rates. Avoid touts on the beach offering overpriced tours.

day_by_day.morning: Join an early morning beach yoga session — many local instructors offer drop-in classes near the beach for $5–10. This is a great way to meet fellow travelers and start the day mindfully with ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or scooter (scooter approx. $5–7/day) and explore the local village and surrounding rice paddies or coastal roads. Visit a local temple if one is nearby — dress respectfully with a sarong (often provided free at temple entrances).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach for sunset — Bali sunsets are spectacular. Find a beachside spot and enjoy the view for free. Afterward, head to a local warung for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or toast with local fruit at a budget café — $3–5.
meals.lunch: Warung lunch — nasi campur (mixed rice plate) with vegetables and protein for $2–4.
meals.dinner: Grilled fish or chicken at a beachside warung — $4–6 including rice and a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is the most budget-friendly way to get around Bali. Always wear a helmet and carry your international driving permit. Petrol is cheap — fill up at a local station rather than roadside bottles.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby famous beach (e.g., Seminyak, Kuta, or Dreamland Beach depending on your resort's location). Arrive early to claim a good spot. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the surf culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the beach town on foot — browse local shops for souvenirs, sarongs, and handmade goods. Practice bargaining respectfully. Visit a free or low-cost local art market.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach or a clifftop viewpoint. Head back toward the resort area and enjoy dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grab a local breakfast on the go — lontong (rice cake with coconut milk soup) or bubur ayam (chicken porridge) for $1–2.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local warung near the beach — budget $3–5 for a full meal.
meals.dinner: Try a slightly nicer local restaurant for a treat — babi guling (suckling pig) or fresh seafood for $6–9.

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and a small day bag. Keep valuables secured when swimming. Petty theft can occur at busy beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga practice — either at the resort, a local studio, or self-guided on the beach. Many studios in Bali offer community classes for $5–8. Spend time journaling or meditating after the session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Hindu temple in the area (entrance fees are usually $1–3 with a sarong rental included). Learn about Balinese culture and observe daily offerings (canang sari). Walk through the surrounding village.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak fire dance performance if available nearby — tickets are usually $8–12 and offer a stunning cultural experience at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl or local fruit platter at a budget health café — $4–5.
meals.lunch: Local warung — gado-gado (peanut sauce salad with tofu and tempeh) for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Dinner near the cultural performance venue — local Indonesian cuisine for $4–6.

day_by_day.notes: Book Kecak dance tickets in advance or ask your hotel to assist. Wear a sarong and sash when entering temples — these are often provided. Respect local customs and ceremonies.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at a quieter, less touristy beach near your resort. Enjoy snorkeling if equipment is available to rent cheaply ($5–8). Look for colorful fish and coral close to shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxing afternoon. Use the resort pool if available, or take a nap and read. Alternatively, explore a local waterfall or nature spot nearby by scooter.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or prepare a light meal using ingredients from a local market — visit a traditional pasar (market) and pick up fresh tropical fruits, tempeh, and local snacks. Great budget-saving option.

meals.breakfast: Warung breakfast — fried egg, rice, and tea for $1.50–2.
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit and snacks from the local market — $2–3.
meals.dinner: Self-prepared or simple warung dinner — $3–5.

day_by_day.notes: Visiting a traditional market is a great cultural experience. Go early in the morning for the freshest produce. Bring small bills for easy transactions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided or self-guided sunrise hike to a nearby hill or coastal viewpoint. Pack water and snacks. The warm weather (25°C) makes early morning the best time for outdoor activities. Enjoy panoramic views of the Bali coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return and rest. Spend the afternoon doing a longer yoga session — look for a 90-minute Vinyasa or Yin yoga class at a local studio ($8–12). Many studios are beginner-friendly.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a local night market (pasar malam) for street food and local goods. Try various street food snacks like pisang goreng (fried banana), martabak, and fresh juice.

meals.breakfast: Packed snacks and fruit brought from the market — $2.
meals.lunch: Post-hike warung meal — nasi goreng with egg for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Street food feast at the night market — sample 3–4 dishes for $4–6 total.

day_by_day.notes: Midpoint of the trip — great time to reflect on your budget spending. Check your expenses and adjust if needed. Stay hydrated in the Bali heat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a famous Bali beach (e.g., Padang Padang, Balangan, or Green Bowl Beach) — these are known for their natural beauty and are less commercialized. Hike down to the beach and enjoy swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on the beach, read, or practice yoga on the sand. Explore the rock formations and tide pools. Take photos of the stunning coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the resort and enjoy a relaxed dinner. Treat yourself to a traditional Balinese massage — many budget spas offer 60-minute massages for $8–12.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the resort — eggs, toast, and coffee for $3–4.
meals.lunch: Beachside warung — fresh coconut and a simple rice dish for $3–4.
meals.dinner: Local restaurant dinner — try ayam betutu (slow-cooked spiced chicken) for $5–7.

day_by_day.notes: Some of Bali's best beaches require a short hike or descent via stairs — wear comfortable footwear. Bring cash as remote beaches may not have ATMs nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and yoga on the beach — self-guided or with a local instructor. Spend time in mindful movement and breathwork as the sun rises over the ocean. This is one of Bali's most magical experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local village or craft area near the resort. Watch artisans making traditional Balinese crafts like woodcarving, batik fabric, or silver jewelry. Purchase meaningful souvenirs directly from makers.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a beachfront dinner as the sun sets. Look for a warung or local restaurant with ocean views — splurge slightly for a beautiful setting.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie and granola at a local health café — $3–4.
meals.lunch: Warung lunch in the village — local curry with rice for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Beachfront warung dinner — grilled prawns or fish with sambal and rice for $6–8.

day_by_day.notes: Supporting local artisans directly helps the community. Avoid mass-produced souvenir shops when possible. Bargain politely but fairly.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day boat trip or snorkeling excursion to a nearby island or reef — many budget group tours are available for $15–25 including equipment. Look for group deals at local tour operators.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the water excursion and relax. Rinse off, rest, and recharge at the resort. Optional: visit a nearby spa for a budget foot or head massage ($5–8).
day_by_day.evening: Join a sunset beach walk or local community event. Check notice boards at the resort or local cafés for free events, live music, or cultural gatherings.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the excursion — simple warung meal for $2.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or food provided on the boat tour — budget $3–5 if not included.
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at a local warung — mixed Indonesian dishes for $4–6.

day_by_day.notes: Book snorkeling/boat tours through local operators rather than hotel desks for better prices. Always check safety equipment before boarding. Apply waterproof sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Attend a longer yoga workshop or beginner's meditation retreat session — many Bali studios offer half-day immersive sessions for $15–25. This is a highlight for yoga enthusiasts and a deeply restorative experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon — wander the local area, visit a beach club for a drink (many have free entry with a minimum spend), or simply relax on the beach with a good book.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a different dining area — walk or scooter to a nearby town or beach strip and try a new cuisine or local specialty you haven't had yet.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before yoga — banana, peanut butter toast, and herbal tea for $2–3.
meals.lunch: Post-workshop healthy café meal — veggie bowl or wrap for $4–5.
meals.dinner: Try a different local restaurant — Balinese black rice pudding or lawar (traditional minced meat salad) for $4–6.

day_by_day.notes: Many yoga studios in Bali have beautiful open-air settings surrounded by nature. Book workshops in advance as popular sessions fill up quickly. Bring a yoga mat or rent one for $1–2.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — spend the morning swimming, surfing, or simply lounging on your favorite beach. Reflect on the trip and soak in the last full day in Bali's warm sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a local market. Pick up Balinese coffee, essential oils, handmade jewelry, or batik fabric as gifts. Pack thoughtfully to stay within luggage limits.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — treat yourself to a slightly nicer local meal to celebrate the trip. Find a restaurant with live traditional Balinese music if possible.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or favorite local café — $3–5.
meals.lunch: Beachside coconut and light snacks — $2–3.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — babi guling or a seafood platter for $8–12. Splurge a little!

day_by_day.notes: Start packing tonight if your flight is early tomorrow. Keep travel documents, passport, and boarding pass easily accessible. Check flight status and arrange airport transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali — wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach or a short quiet meditation. Breathe in the ocean air and appreciate the experience. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, spend remaining hours relaxing at a nearby café or beach. Head to Ngurah Rai International Airport with plenty of time — allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with wonderful memories. Reflect on the incredible beaches, yoga experiences, local food, and cultural richness of the Island of the Gods.

meals.breakfast: Final Balinese breakfast — nasi goreng or fresh fruit at a local warung for $2–3.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or nearby café before departure — $5–8.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight. Use up remaining Rupiah on snacks, bottled water, or last-minute gifts at the airport. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room. Take a short stroll on the resort terrace to enjoy the night ocean breeze.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack or room service at the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid stress upon late-night arrival. Exchange some currency at the airport for initial expenses. Keep the first night light — rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take your first walk along the beachfront to get oriented with the surroundings and soak in the Bali coastal atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the resort's beachfront. Rent a sun lounger, take a dip in the warm Indian Ocean, and explore the immediate beach area. Visit a nearby surf shop to inquire about beginner surf lessons for later in the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby beachside warung (local eatery) for your first authentic Balinese dinner. Watch the sunset from the beach before retiring early to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — enjoy tropical fruits, local rice porridge (bubur), and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a beachside café near the resort — try Nasi Goreng (fried rice) or Mie Goreng (fried noodles)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range beachfront warung — order Grilled Fish with sambal, steamed rice, and fresh coconut water (approx. IDR 80,000–150,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today. Jet lag from a late-night arrival can be significant. Hydrate well and use SPF 50+ sunscreen — Bali's UV index is high even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Join a sunrise beach yoga session — many resorts and local studios near beachfront areas offer 60–90 minute morning yoga classes starting around 07:00. Enjoy the peaceful sound of waves during your practice. Return to the resort for a refreshing shower.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach town on foot or by renting a scooter. Visit a local market to browse handmade crafts, sarongs, and souvenirs. Stop at a traditional Balinese temple near the coast for a cultural introduction — dress respectfully with a sarong.
day_by_day.evening: Join a group sunset yoga session on the beach (many instructors offer this around 17:30–19:00). Afterward, enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — avocado toast, smoothie bowl, or local banana pancakes
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local warung in the market area — try Lawar (mixed vegetables with coconut) or Soto Ayam (chicken soup)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant — order Balinese Babi Guling (suckling pig) or fresh seafood platter (approx. IDR 120,000–200,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: When visiting temples, always wear a sarong and sash — these are often available to borrow or buy at the entrance for a small fee. Respect local customs by staying quiet and not pointing feet toward sacred objects.

day_by_day.morning: Take a beginner or intermediate surf lesson on the beach (approx. IDR 250,000–400,000 for a 2-hour lesson including board and instructor). Bali's warm waters and consistent waves make it ideal for learning. Lessons typically start at 08:00 to catch the best morning conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, relax and recharge with a traditional Balinese massage at a local spa near the resort (approx. IDR 100,000–180,000 for a 60-minute full body massage). Spend the remaining afternoon reading or napping on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the resort's nearest town for dinner. Visit a lively night market or restaurant strip for a casual, social evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pre-surf breakfast at the resort — eggs, toast, fruit, and coffee to fuel the lesson
meals.lunch: Post-surf lunch at a surf shack or casual café — try a Bali bowl (rice, tempeh, veggies, egg) or fresh fruit smoothie
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — try Bebek Betutu (slow-cooked duck in Balinese spices) or grilled satay skewers with peanut sauce

day_by_day.notes: Book your surf lesson the day before to secure a spot. Apply waterproof sunscreen before entering the water. If you have no surfing experience, opt for a 2-hour beginner group lesson for better value.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud — Bali's cultural heartland (approximately 1.5–2 hours from the coast by private driver, approx. IDR 300,000–500,000 round trip). Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in the morning to explore ancient temples surrounded by playful long-tailed macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's famous Tegalalang Rice Terraces — walk the terraced paths and enjoy panoramic views of lush green paddies. Stop at local artisan workshops along Ubud's main street to see wood carving, silver jewelry making, and batik fabric creation.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud Temple (approx. IDR 100,000–150,000 per person) — typically held at 19:00. Drive back to the resort after the performance.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range restaurant in Ubud — try Warung Ibu Oka for Babi Guling or a local warung for Nasi Campur (mixed rice plate)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ubud before heading back or stop at a roadside warung on the return journey — try Gado-Gado (peanut sauce salad) or Tempeh Manis

day_by_day.notes: Hire a reliable private driver for the Ubud day trip — negotiate the price the evening before. Keep a small bag of belongings secure at the Monkey Forest as monkeys are known to grab loose items. Book the Kecak dance tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga class at a local studio or on the beach at 07:00. Focus on a restorative or vinyasa session to balance the activity of previous days. Spend time journaling or meditating on the beach after class.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling excursion from a nearby beach — rent snorkel gear (approx. IDR 50,000–80,000) or join a guided boat snorkeling trip to a nearby reef (approx. IDR 200,000–350,000). Explore colorful coral reefs and tropical fish in Bali's warm, clear waters.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Enjoy the resort pool or beachfront area at sunset. Dine at the resort restaurant for a comfortable, convenient evening.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast — banana, granola, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Post-snorkeling lunch at a beachside café — fresh grilled fish, coconut rice, and a tropical juice
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — choose a mid-range set menu or à la carte Balinese dishes (approx. IDR 150,000–250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If snorkeling independently, always go with a buddy and avoid touching coral reefs. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect the marine ecosystem. Check weather conditions before booking boat trips.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most iconic sea temples perched on a rocky outcrop in the ocean (approx. 45–60 minutes from most beachfront areas). Arrive early (08:00) to beat the crowds and enjoy the dramatic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Uluwatu Temple on Bali's southern Bukit Peninsula — a clifftop temple with breathtaking views 70 meters above the Indian Ocean. Explore the surrounding cliffs and watch surfers tackle the famous Uluwatu waves below.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Kecak Fire Dance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset (approx. 18:00, IDR 150,000 per person) — performed against the backdrop of the ocean and setting sun. Have dinner at one of the clifftop restaurants in the Uluwatu area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before an early departure
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tanah Lot — try a local warung serving Nasi Goreng or fresh coconut and snacks
meals.dinner: Dinner at a clifftop restaurant near Uluwatu — seafood BBQ platter or grilled prawns with Balinese sambal (approx. IDR 150,000–280,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for temple visits. Sarongs are mandatory at both temples. Beware of monkeys at Uluwatu — secure sunglasses, hats, and bags. The Uluwatu Kecak dance is considered one of the best in Bali — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and wellness morning — start with a 60-minute beach meditation or gentle yoga session at sunrise. Treat yourself to a traditional Balinese boreh body scrub and flower bath at a local spa (approx. IDR 200,000–350,000 for a 90-minute package).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby coastal village on foot or by bicycle. Visit local warungs, interact with residents, and discover authentic Balinese daily life away from tourist areas. Stop at a local coconut stall for a refreshing drink.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class experience — join a Balinese cooking class (approx. IDR 350,000–500,000 per person) where you'll learn to make traditional dishes like Satay, Lawar, and black rice pudding. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh fruit platter at a health café near the resort
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a village warung during your afternoon exploration — try local Jaja (traditional Balinese snacks) and coconut water
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the cooking class — a fun and delicious way to end the evening

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance. Most classes include a market visit in the morning — check if your chosen class offers this add-on. The spa boreh scrub uses traditional spices like ginger, turmeric, and clove — inform staff of any skin sensitivities.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Mount Batur — an active volcano in Bali's highlands. Join a guided sunrise trek (wake up at 02:00, depart 03:00, approx. IDR 350,000–600,000 per person including guide). Reach the summit by sunrise for panoramic views of the crater lake and surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the volcano and visit the natural hot springs at the base of Mount Batur (Toya Devasya or similar, approx. IDR 150,000–200,000) to soak tired muscles. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Early, restful evening at the resort. Enjoy a light dinner and get to bed early to recover from the early wake-up.

meals.breakfast: Pre-trek snack provided by the guide (usually banana and biscuits) or pack your own energy bars
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near the hot springs — try Nasi Campur or Mie Goreng
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort or a nearby warung — opt for something easy like soup, steamed fish, or vegetable dishes

day_by_day.notes: The Mount Batur trek requires a 02:00–03:00 departure for sunrise. Book your guide the day before through your hotel or a reputable local tour operator. Wear layers — the summit is cool at pre-dawn. Bring a headlamp, water, and light snacks. The trek is moderate difficulty — suitable for average fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the volcano trek. Sleep in, enjoy a slow resort breakfast, and spend the morning at the beach or pool. Optional: gentle stretching or restorative yoga session at 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby water temple such as Pura Tirta Empul — a sacred Hindu water temple where locals perform purification rituals in natural spring pools. Observe or respectfully participate in the melukat (purification) ritual (entrance approx. IDR 50,000).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar — enjoy Bali's famous sunset with a Bintang beer, fresh coconut, or tropical mocktail. Dinner at a lively mid-range restaurant with live music.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — reward yourself after the volcano trek with a hearty meal
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tirta Empul — local warung serving Nasi Goreng, fresh spring rolls, or tofu satay
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant with live Balinese music — try a seafood curry, grilled barramundi, or a vegetarian rijsttafel (rice table) spread

day_by_day.notes: At Tirta Empul, wear modest clothing and a sarong. If you choose to participate in the purification ritual, follow the proper sequence of pools and observe what locals do. Photography inside the bathing pools is discouraged out of respect.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach yoga session followed by a paddleboarding lesson on calm morning waters (approx. IDR 150,000–250,000 for 1 hour with instruction). Paddleboarding is a great low-impact activity that combines balance, core strength, and ocean enjoyment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local batik or silver jewelry workshop in a nearby artisan village. Try your hand at creating your own batik fabric or silver pendant as a hands-on cultural souvenir experience (approx. IDR 150,000–300,000 depending on activity).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style indulgent dinner at one of the area's best mid-range restaurants. Dress up slightly and enjoy a more refined Balinese dining experience with multiple courses.

meals.breakfast: Pre-yoga light breakfast — banana, peanut butter toast, and green tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at the artisan village — fresh local food at a family-run warung, try Pepes Ikan (fish in banana leaf) or Ayam Betutu (slow-cooked chicken)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-regarded mid-range Balinese restaurant — enjoy a set menu featuring multiple traditional dishes, ending with Dadar Gulung (green crepe with coconut filling) for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Check tidal conditions before paddleboarding — morning is usually the calmest time. The batik workshop is a wonderful way to create a unique, personal souvenir. Most workshops provide all materials and guidance.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — spend quality time on the beach, swim in the ocean, and reflect on your Bali journey. Optional: join a final morning yoga class to close your yoga practice for the trip with intention.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a local market — pick up Balinese textiles, wood carvings, essential oils, locally made chocolate, or coffee as gifts. Visit a local café for a final Bali coffee experience — try Kopi Luwak or traditional Balinese Kopi Tubruk.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at a beachfront restaurant — choose a table with ocean views and toast to a wonderful trip. Enjoy the last Bali sunset before packing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — enjoy every item on the menu one last time
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a market café or food stall while shopping — try Martabak (stuffed pancake) or fresh fruit skewers
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a beachfront restaurant — splurge slightly on a seafood feast: lobster, prawns, calamari, and grilled fish with Balinese sambal and steamed rice (approx. IDR 250,000–400,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing this evening. Set aside any liquids, sarongs, or items that need to go into checked luggage. Confirm your departure transfer booking and flight check-in details. Keep some IDR cash for tips and last-minute expenses.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the beach — wake up early for one last magical Bali sunrise. Take photos, breathe in the ocean air, and cherish the moment. Return to the resort for a final breakfast and complete packing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure time, store luggage with the concierge and enjoy the resort pool or beach for a final few hours. Arrange your airport transfer — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for traffic and check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for Ngurah Rai International Airport. Complete check-in, customs, and security. Browse the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute Bali souvenirs — Balinese coffee, chocolate, or local spice kits make great gifts.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy tropical fruits, local pastries, and a farewell Bali coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort before checkout or grab a meal at the airport — try the airport's local food court for one final taste of Indonesian cuisine
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Bali's traffic can be unpredictable — always allow extra time for the airport journey, especially during peak hours (07:00–09:00 and 17:00–20:00). Carry all important documents — passport, boarding pass, travel insurance — in your hand luggage. Selamat jalan — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. A private luxury transfer with a dedicated concierge will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort, Bali. Check in, enjoy a welcome drink and a light late-night amenity platter prepared by the resort, then settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In transit
meals.lunch: N/A – In transit
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity platter and herbal teas arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the resort. Request a late check-in amenity package in advance. Unpack lightly and rest – a full itinerary begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely in-suite breakfast with ocean views. At 9:30 AM, join a private sunrise beach yoga session led by the resort's resident yoga instructor directly on the beachfront – a gentle flow to awaken the body after travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort's private beach. Enjoy complimentary water sports (paddleboarding, snorkeling) arranged by the resort's beach butler. Take a dip in the infinity pool overlooking the Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the resort's clifftop bar, then dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring modern Indonesian cuisine with premium seafood.

meals.breakfast: In-suite private breakfast with tropical fruits, pastries, eggs to order, fresh juices, and Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's beach club – grilled catch of the day, fresh salads, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Signature restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort – tasting menu featuring Balinese spiced lobster, wagyu beef rendang, and artisan desserts paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Keep the pace relaxed. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: 7:00 AM private Vinyasa yoga class on the resort's open-air yoga pavilion overlooking the ocean. Follow with a traditional Balinese spa treatment – a 90-minute warm stone massage and floral bath ritual at the resort's luxury spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour to the iconic Tanah Lot Sea Temple, one of Bali's most sacred and photogenic landmarks perched on a rocky outcrop. Explore the temple grounds with a knowledgeable private guide who explains its spiritual significance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private beachfront dinner under the stars – a bespoke dining experience arranged by the resort's butler service with a custom menu, candles, and ambient Balinese music.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant buffet breakfast featuring international and Balinese selections – nasi goreng, fresh tropical fruits, smoked salmon, artisan breads
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium warung near Tanah Lot – Jimbaran-style grilled seafood platters with sambal matah and steamed rice
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner experience – chef's custom five-course menu with champagne and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is approximately 30–45 minutes from most beachfront resorts in southern Bali. Sunset at Tanah Lot is spectacular – time your visit accordingly. Wear modest clothing to enter temple grounds.

day_by_day.morning: 6:30 AM early morning beach meditation and pranayama breathing session with the resort's wellness instructor. Afterward, take a private surf lesson with a certified instructor on the resort's nearby beach break – perfect for beginners and intermediates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the upscale Seminyak area for luxury boutique shopping – browse high-end Balinese designers, artisan jewelry, and premium homeware stores. Explore the chic streets of Seminyak at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at Ku De Ta or Potato Head Beach Club – iconic Seminyak venues offering world-class cocktails and ocean views. Dinner at a celebrated Seminyak fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light healthy breakfast at the resort – acai bowls, green smoothies, avocado toast, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Lucciola, Seminyak – renowned beachfront Italian-Mediterranean restaurant with fresh pasta, seafood, and Bali's best sea views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Métis Restaurant, Seminyak – acclaimed French-Mediterranean cuisine in a stunning colonial villa setting with an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Seminyak is approximately 20–30 minutes from the resort depending on traffic. Use the resort's private car service for all transfers. Book Métis well in advance as it is very popular.

day_by_day.morning: 7:00 AM private Yin yoga and mindfulness meditation session at the resort's beachfront pavilion. After breakfast, depart for a private day trip to Uluwatu – visit the dramatic clifftop Uluwatu Temple perched 70 meters above the Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Uluwatu area's world-famous surf beaches – Padang Padang and Bingin Beach. Even as a non-surfer, these beaches are breathtaking. Enjoy a private snorkeling excursion in the crystal-clear waters near the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset – a UNESCO-recognized cultural spectacle performed against a dramatic ocean backdrop. Dinner at a premium clifftop restaurant in Uluwatu.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – eggs benedict, smoked salmon bagels, fresh tropical juices, and Balinese herbal tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Single Fin, Uluwatu – iconic clifftop beach bar and restaurant with spectacular surf views, fresh seafood burgers, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sundays Beach Club or Omnia Dayclub Bali – premium clifftop dining with modern Asian-fusion cuisine and panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: The Kecak Dance begins at sunset (approximately 6:00–7:00 PM). Book tickets in advance. Wear a sarong at the temple – they are available to borrow at the entrance. The Uluwatu area is about 45–60 minutes from the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning dedicated to wellness – begin with a 7:00 AM Ashtanga yoga practice, followed by a two-hour Balinese Royal Lulur body treatment at the resort spa (traditional Javanese royal scrub, herbal compress, and milk bath). This treatment was historically used by Javanese royalty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon at the resort's private beach and infinity pool. Arrange a private beach cabana with butler service – enjoy curated snacks, fresh coconuts, and chilled towels while reading or simply unwinding.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-villa dining experience – the resort's private chef prepares a bespoke Balinese feast in your suite with a dedicated butler, ambient lighting, and a curated Balinese playlist.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast – fresh papaya, granola with coconut yogurt, eggs any style, freshly baked croissants, and Balinese single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside gourmet lunch – lobster rolls, truffle fries, fresh ceviche, and sparkling water with citrus
meals.dinner: Private in-villa Balinese feast – bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck), suckling pig (babi guling), satay lilit, lawar salad, steamed rice, and traditional jaja sweets

day_by_day.notes: This is a full rest and rejuvenation day. No off-resort travel required. Communicate any dietary preferences or allergies to the resort chef 24 hours in advance for the private dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (7:00 AM) for a full-day private excursion to Ubud – Bali's cultural and spiritual heartland. Begin with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary and the ancient Pura Dalem Agung Padangtegal temple within.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's world-famous art scene – visit the Neka Art Museum and the ARMA (Agung Rai Museum of Art) to discover traditional Balinese paintings and sculptures. Browse the Ubud Art Market for premium handcrafted souvenirs, silk scarves, and silver jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Legong or Barong dance performance at the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) – an elegant royal setting for classical Balinese dance. Dinner at one of Ubud's finest restaurants before the private drive back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – continental spread with pastries, fruits, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Locavore, Ubud – one of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, celebrating local Balinese ingredients in a contemporary fine-dining format (advance reservation essential)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mozaic Restaurant Gastronomique, Ubud – acclaimed garden restaurant offering an innovative French-Indonesian tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1.5 hours from the beachfront area. Reserve Locavore and Mozaic weeks in advance – both are highly sought after. Bring light layers as Ubud's elevation makes it slightly cooler in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: 7:00 AM private sunrise yoga on the beach – a dynamic Vinyasa flow timed to catch the golden hour over the ocean. After breakfast, join a private guided snorkeling or scuba diving excursion to nearby coral reefs – Bali's underwater world is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure at the resort. Indulge in a 60-minute couples' or solo aromatherapy massage at the spa. Alternatively, take a private stand-up paddleboarding lesson along the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cruise – arrange a private luxury boat charter for a 2-hour sunset sailing experience along Bali's southern coastline with champagne, canapés, and a dedicated crew.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – full Balinese breakfast featuring bubur sumsum (rice porridge), jukut urap (vegetable salad), fresh fruit platter, and herbal jamu shots
meals.lunch: Light lunch aboard the dive boat or back at the resort beach club – fresh sashimi, grilled prawns, and tropical fruit salad
meals.dinner: Dinner at Jimbaran Bay seafood beach restaurants – choose from premium operators like Menega Café or Sundara at Four Seasons for a candlelit beachfront seafood feast

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the sunset cruise booking 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Jimbaran Bay is approximately 20–30 minutes away and is famous for its fresh grilled seafood on the beach at sunset.

day_by_day.morning: 7:00 AM Kundalini yoga and sound healing session at the resort's wellness pavilion using singing bowls and gongs – a deeply restorative practice. After breakfast, depart for a private tour of the Besakih Temple complex – Bali's Mother Temple, the largest and most sacred Hindu temple on the island, set on the slopes of Mount Agung.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Kintamani volcanic highlands for breathtaking views of Mount Batur and the vast caldera lake. Enjoy the scenery from a premium viewpoint restaurant overlooking the volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by private car. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a private outdoor jacuzzi session in your suite, followed by a light in-room dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – smoothie bowls, chia pudding, poached eggs on sourdough, fresh juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lakeview Restaurant, Kintamani – premium restaurant perched above the caldera with panoramic volcano views and an international buffet featuring local Balinese specialties
meals.dinner: In-suite private dining – light and healthy menu: seared tuna tataki, miso soup, steamed vegetables, Japanese-style rice, and fresh fruit sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Besakih and Kintamani are approximately 2 hours from the beachfront resort. This is a full-day excursion – depart by 8:00 AM. Wear respectful attire at Besakih Temple and hire an official temple guide on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated spa and wellness morning – begin with a 7:00 AM restorative yoga Nidra (yogic sleep) session, followed by a three-hour Balinese Healing Journey at the resort spa: traditional healer consultation, herbal body mask, hot stone therapy, and a flower petal bath.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class with the resort's executive chef – learn to prepare authentic Balinese dishes including satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding using fresh market ingredients. A fun and immersive cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class at a private dinner in the resort's garden terrace. Toast your culinary achievements with a bottle of premium Champagne.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-spa breakfast – green smoothie, overnight oats, fresh papaya with lime, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Post-spa healthy lunch at the resort – Buddha bowls with tempeh, roasted vegetables, tahini, and quinoa; fresh pressed juices
meals.dinner: Private garden terrace dinner featuring the dishes prepared in the afternoon cooking class, with Champagne and a curated dessert selection from the resort's pastry chef

day_by_day.notes: Inform the resort spa team of any health conditions before the healing journey. The cooking class typically lasts 2–3 hours and is a wonderful way to take a piece of Bali home with you. Request a recipe booklet from the chef.

day_by_day.morning: 7:00 AM beach yoga – a slow, meditative Hatha practice on the shoreline as the tide comes in. After breakfast, embark on a private guided tour to the Tegallalang Rice Terraces near Ubud – one of Bali's most iconic UNESCO-recognized landscapes. Walk through the lush emerald terraces with your private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a premium Balinese silver jewelry workshop in Celuk village – watch master craftsmen at work and commission a bespoke piece of jewelry as a personal memento of your trip. Continue to the Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave) – an ancient archaeological site from the 9th century.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a romantic sunset at the beach. Arrange a private bonfire on the beach with the resort's butler service – enjoy cocktails, light bites, and the sound of the waves as the sky turns golden.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – eggs royale, smoked salmon, avocado, fresh fruit, pastries, and freshly brewed Kopi Luwak (world's rarest coffee)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant overlooking the Tegallalang Rice Terraces – fresh Balinese cuisine with sweeping green views
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire dinner – gourmet canapés, charcuterie board, fresh seafood skewers grilled over the fire, and artisan chocolates with dessert wine

day_by_day.notes: Kopi Luwak (civet coffee) is a unique Balinese specialty – request it specifically from the resort. The Tegallalang terraces can be busy in the morning; your private guide will navigate the best routes. The bonfire experience must be arranged 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning – 7:00 AM sunrise meditation on the beach, then a gentle restorative yoga session to honor the body before travel. After breakfast, enjoy a farewell spa treatment – a 60-minute Balinese massage and scalp treatment to leave you completely refreshed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon of leisure at the resort – swim, sunbathe, and soak in every last moment of the beachfront paradise. Take a final walk along the beach and collect a few shells as natural souvenirs. Visit the resort's boutique for any last-minute premium gifts or products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's finest restaurant – a celebratory meal to mark an extraordinary 13-day journey. Share highlights with travel companions over exceptional food and wine.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast in-suite – a lavish spread of all your favorite items from the past 12 days, curated by the butler
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – fresh sushi platter, miso soup, edamame, and tropical sorbet
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's signature restaurant – premium seven-course degustation menu with wine pairing, live ambient music, and a personalized farewell dessert

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout if your flight departs late on Day 13. Pack carefully and leave valuables in the in-room safe until departure. Settle any outstanding resort charges this evening to streamline tomorrow's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – if time permits before checkout, enjoy one last sunrise beach walk or a quiet meditation by the ocean. Savor a final breakfast at the resort at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, Bali. The resort's dedicated concierge will assist with luggage and coordinate your private luxury airport transfer. Depart for Ngurah Rai International Airport with beautiful memories and a heart full of Bali's magic.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of beaches, yoga, culture, cuisine, and pure luxury.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort – choose your favorites from the menu; savor the last moments of your beachfront paradise
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport's premium lounge or an early meal at the resort before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your checkout time and airport transfer with the resort concierge the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for airport procedures. Keep travel documents, valuables, and any purchased art or jewelry in your carry-on luggage.
